sources.scope_note: Re-verified live 2026-10-16: page text-identical to 2026-10-13 (2027 plan-year requested AND approved rate-change tables; 15 individual, 16 small-group companies; two-phase rate review text intact). New page-level observation 2026-10-16: request-to-approved divergence varies in direction — approved below requested (e.g., Ambetter Health of PA individual 40.90% -> 35.13%; Oscar individual 15.39% -> 1.38%), approved above requested (Health Partners Plans individual 15.90% -> 18.35%; Keystone Health Plan East individual 14.68% -> 15.98%; QCC Insurance individual 19.88% -> 21.31%), approved equal to requested (e.g., Independence Assurance small group 8.95% -> 8.95%), and '0.00% New Plan' rows with no prior premium to change (Ambetter Health Solutions of PA). Rate-change % and coverage-map links only: no premium amounts, no provider networks, no behavioral-health reimbursement figures. Market coverage area and premium filings do not prove a provider's network participation or behavioral-health reimbursement. sources.title: The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA)
sources.program: Private health insurance; group and individual markets
sources.scope_note: Federal parity requirements; confirm applicability (plan type, market, state law) before modeling any rule. 2024 final rules (HHS/Labor/Treasury, 2024-09-09) and CAA-2021 NQTL comparative-analysis duty noted from page; linked regulations not yet read. Re-verified 2026-11-01: page content unchanged since 2026-10-14 (and 2026-10-12) — same 145-line text, same seven section headers, Fact Sheets & FAQs and Regulations and Guidance still empty. NEW page-level observation: the per-classification mechanics not covered by the earlier workbook scenes — the substantially-all/predominant test applied separately to six classifications, MH/SUD benefits required in all classifications where medical/surgical benefits are provided, cumulative financial requirements (deductibles, out-of-pocket limits) combining both benefit types within a classification, and scope/duration standards (geographic limits, facility-type limits, network adequacy) subject to NQTL parity. NEW page-level angle shipped as consumer: the non-mandate rule — MHPAEA does NOT require MH/SUD coverage, the ACA EHB requirement supplies coverage in non-grandfathered individual/small-group plans, MHPAEA applies to small-group plans only indirectly via EHB, small employer generally 1-50 (states may expand to 1-100), and some states may be stricter than federal law (not enumerated on the page).
